title: How do you turn a grey clay render into a photorealistic product video?
description: Hand the model two references with two different jobs: one carries structure only, the other carries look only. Then say which reference owns which job.
alt: Vaporswift Reel — a grey clay whiskey glass becoming a photoreal cut-crystal glass with amber liquid and condensation

faq.q: How do you use two reference images in an AI video prompt?
faq.a: Assign each one a job and say so explicitly. Reference 1 carries structure only — camera angle, composition, object placement and scale. Reference 2 carries look only — material, colour, lighting direction. The model needs to be told which reference owns which, or it averages them.

faq.q: Why does my clay render stay grey in the output?
faq.a: Because feeding a clay image as a reference makes the model want to keep some of it. You have to state that the output contains none: 'no clay or grey untextured surfaces in the output.'
